_readme: Speak-stage content. Edit freely. Each phrase: jp (as written, kanji OK), kana (reading in kana, used for speech matching), romaji, en, note. Role-play lines: speaker 'them' (app speaks) or 'you' (Eliz answers; first option listed is the correct one, the app shuffles them). Progress is keyed by unit id + jp text, so editing a phrase's jp resets progress for that one phrase only.

phrases.note: The all-purpose daytime hello. The last は is pronounced "wa" here.
Polite form. With friends and family, just おはよう (ohayō).
Use after dark. Again, the final は is "wa".
Only for the very first time you meet someone. It usually opens a self-introduction.
Your name + です. Japanese speakers usually leave out わたしは ("I") when it's obvious. Your name in katakana is エリズ.

phrases.jp: よろしくお願いします
phrases.kana: よろしくおねがいします
phrases.en: Nice to meet you / I look forward to working with you
phrases.note: Closes a self-introduction (after はじめまして… です). Also used when asking someone a favor.
Used when you haven't seen someone in a while, not as a daily "how's it going".
The standard reply. You can add おかげさまで (okagesama de, "thanks to you") to sound extra polite.

phrases.jp: ありがとうございます
phrases.kana: ありがとうございます
phrases.note: Safe with everyone. With close friends, ありがとう (arigatō) is enough.
Friends only. With people you don't know well, say それでは、また (soredewa, mata).

roleplay.title: Meeting Shota's friend Yuki
roleplay.setting: You're at a café and Shota introduces you to his friend Yuki.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: はじめまして。ゆきです。
lines.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Yuki.

options.jp: はじめまして。エリズです。
options.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Eliz.

options.jp: おはようございます。ゆきです。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: よろしくお願いします。

options.jp: よろしくお願いします。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: 日本語、上手ですね！

lines.speaker: you
lines.note: Accepting a compliment directly can sound boastful. いいえ、まだまだです is the classic humble reply.

options.en: Oh no, I still have a long way to go.

units.title: Yes, no & polite basics
units.summary: The little words that get you through any conversation.

phrases.note: Also means "I'm listening" or "here you go" when handing something over.
Fairly direct. In conversation people often soften it, e.g. いえいえ when brushing off thanks.
Your most useful word: getting a server's attention, squeezing past someone, a light apology, even a humble "thanks".
A personal apology, softer and more heartfelt than すみません. Not used to get attention.
Also a polite way to decline: offered a bag or a refill you don't want? 大丈夫です.
Polite and everyday. Staff will say the extra-formal かしこまりました.

phrases.en: I don't understand / I don't know
phrases.note: Start with すみません、 to soften it.

phrases.jp: もう一度お願いします
phrases.kana: もういちどおねがいします
phrases.note: Your lifeline when someone speaks too fast.

phrases.jp: ゆっくりお願いします
phrases.kana: ゆっくりおねがいします
phrases.note: Pair it with もう一度: もう一度、ゆっくりお願いします.

phrases.kana: えいごをはなせますか
phrases.note: 英語が話せますか (with が) is equally common.

roleplay.title: Someone stops you on the street
roleplay.setting: A friendly local stops you and starts talking quickly.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Local
lines.jp: すみません、ちょっといいですか？
lines.en: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

options.jp: こんばんは、エリズです。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Local
lines.jp: この近くに郵便局はありますか？
lines.romaji: Kono chikaku ni yūbinkyoku wa arimasu ka?
lines.en: Is there a post office near here?

lines.speaker: you
lines.prompt: That was fast. Ask them to repeat it.

options.jp: すみません、もう一度お願いします。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Local
lines.jp: 郵便局です。この近くにありますか？
lines.romaji: Yūbinkyoku desu. Kono chikaku ni arimasu ka?
lines.en: A post office. Is there one nearby?

lines.speaker: you
lines.prompt: You don't know. Say so politely.

options.jp: すみません、わかりません。
よろしくお願いします。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Local
lines.jp: 大丈夫です。ありがとうございます！

units.title: At a café or restaurant
units.summary: Getting a table, ordering, and paying.

phrases.note: You'll hear this at the door. Answer with the number of people, or just hold up fingers.
One person is 一人 (hitori), three is 三人 (san-nin).

phrases.jp: メニューをお願いします
phrases.kana: めにゅーをおねがいします
phrases.note: Add すみません、 first to get a server's attention.

phrases.kana: おすすめはなんですか
phrases.note: Servers love this question and it often gets you the best dish.
Point at the menu photo. Works everywhere.

phrases.jp: コーヒーを一つお願いします
phrases.kana: こーひーをひとつおねがいします
phrases.note: ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ (one, two, three) count most things you order.
Water is usually free. The お makes it sound polite and soft.
Like a small thank-you before the first bite. Everyone says it, even alone.
With friends, just おいしい！

phrases.en: Thank you for the meal (after eating)
phrases.note: Say it after the meal, and to the staff as you leave. It's always appreciated.

phrases.kana: おかいけいおねがいします
phrases.note: In many places you pay at the register by the door, not at the table.

roleplay.title: Coffee for two
roleplay.setting: You walk into a small café with Shota.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: いらっしゃいませ！何名様ですか？

lines.speaker: you
lines.prompt: Tell them it's two of you.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: ご注文はお決まりですか？

options.jp: コーヒーを一つお願いします。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: かしこまりました。

options.jp: すみません、お会計お願いします。
すみません、いただきます。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: ありがとうございました！

units.title: Finding your way
units.summary: Asking where things are and understanding the answer.

phrases.note: [thing] は どこですか works for anything you're looking for.
駅 (eki) = train station.

phrases.jp: この近くにコンビニはありますか
phrases.kana: このちかくにこんびにはありますか
phrases.romaji: kono chikaku ni konbini wa arimasu ka
phrases.en: Is there a convenience store nearby?
phrases.note: Swap コンビニ for any place: 郵便局 (post office), ATM, 薬局 (pharmacy).
The small っ is a tiny pause: mas-sugu.
右に曲がってください = please turn right.
Tip: 右 (migi) and 左 (hidari) are easy to mix up at first. Say them with a gesture.
ここ (here), そこ (there, near you), あそこ (over there, away from both of us).

phrases.kana: ここからとおいですか
phrases.note: The opposite of 遠い (far) is 近い (chikai, near).

phrases.jp: 歩いて五分ぐらいです
phrases.kana: あるいてごふんぐらいです
phrases.note: ぐらい (or くらい) = "about". You'll hear this kind of answer often.

phrases.jp: 地図で教えてもらえますか
phrases.kana: ちずでおしえてもらえますか
phrases.en: Could you show me on the map?
phrases.note: Hold up your phone map while you ask. Much easier than following spoken directions.

roleplay.title: Looking for the station
roleplay.setting: You're lost near Shibuya and need the station.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Passer-by
lines.jp: はい？

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Passer-by
lines.jp: あの信号を右に曲がってください。
lines.romaji: Ano shingō o migi ni magatte kudasai.
lines.en: Please turn right at that traffic light.

options.en: The restroom is on the left.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Passer-by
lines.jp: いいえ、歩いて五分ぐらいですよ。
lines.romaji: Iie, aruite go-fun gurai desu yo.
lines.en: No, it's about five minutes on foot.

options.jp: ありがとうございます。

phrases.note: You'll hear it the moment you walk in. No need to reply; a smile or small nod is perfect.
In casual speech it shortens to 見てるだけです (miteru dake desu).
Point at the item. Prices are usually shown, but this is handy at markets.
円 (en) = yen. Japanese counts in units of 10,000 (万, man), so 10,000 yen is 一万円 (ichiman en).
Watch the sound changes: 300 is さんびゃく (sanbyaku), 600 is ろっぴゃく (roppyaku).
The most common banknote.
3,000 softens to さんぜん (sanzen), and 8,000 is はっせん (hassen).

phrases.jp: 試着してもいいですか
phrases.kana: しちゃくしてもいいですか
phrases.romaji: shichaku shite mo ii desu ka
phrases.note: 〜てもいいですか = "May I …?" Very useful pattern.
Literally "I'll go with this". Also works when choosing from a menu.

phrases.kana: かーどではらえますか
phrases.note: Most shops take cards, but small restaurants and shrines may be cash only.

phrases.kana: ふくろはだいじょうぶです
phrases.note: Bags usually cost a few yen now, so cashiers will ask.

roleplay.title: Buying a scarf
roleplay.setting: You find a scarf you love at a small shop.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: いらっしゃいませ。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: 三千円です。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: 袋はお付けしますか？

lines.speaker: you
lines.prompt: Politely say you don't need one.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Staff
lines.jp: ありがとうございました。

units.title: Likes & small talk
units.summary: Talking about what you do and what you love.

phrases.note: A classic getting-to-know-you question.

phrases.kana: しゅみはりょうりです
phrases.note: Swap in your own: 写真 (shashin, photography), 旅行 (ryokō, travel), 絵 (e, drawing).
好き (suki) = like. Note it uses が, not を.
[thing] が好きです is the pattern for anything you like.

phrases.jp: 映画を見るのが好きです
phrases.kana: えいがをみるのがすきです
phrases.romaji: eiga o miru no ga suki desu
phrases.note: Verb + のが好きです = "I like doing …".
Job + です. Graphic designer is グラフィックデザイナー.

phrases.jp: 日本語を勉強しています
phrases.kana: にほんごをべんきょうしています
phrases.note: People will be delighted to hear this, and often slow down for you.
も (mo) = also. Casual: 私も！
The ね invites agreement. It's warm and keeps the conversation going.

phrases.kana: しゅうまつはなにをしますか
phrases.romaji: shūmatsu wa nani o shimasu ka
phrases.en: What do you do on weekends?
phrases.note: Great follow-up question when talk slows down.

roleplay.title: Chatting with Yuki
roleplay.setting: Yuki wants to get to know you better.

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: エリズさんのお仕事は何ですか？
lines.romaji: Erizu-san no o-shigoto wa nan desu ka?
lines.en: What do you do for work, Eliz?

options.jp: デザイナーが好きですか。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: へえ、すごい！趣味は何ですか？
lines.romaji: Hē, sugoi! Shumi wa nan desu ka?
lines.en: Wow, amazing! What are your hobbies?

options.jp: 音楽を一つお願いします。

lines.speaker: them
lines.name: Yuki
lines.jp: 私も音楽が好きです！
lines.romaji: Watashi mo ongaku ga suki desu!
